narrative_passages.title: Nuh calls his people
narrative_passages.treatment_reason: Read only; no one is shown.

summary_for_children: Surah Nuh tells how Nuh called his people for a very long time, by day and by night, telling them to ask Allah's forgiveness so He would send rain, gardens and rivers.
world_title: Nuh's Call by Night and Day
environment_concept: The promise of 71:10-12 told through the land: three dry fields that turn green when the child brings rain clouds, a riverbed that fills beside fruit trees, two pedestals for the moon as "a [reflected] light" and the sun as "a burning lamp" (71:16), and roads winding through wide hills (71:19-20). Nuh and his people are never shown; the seven heavens are not pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: A village square, private courtyards, rain clouds over gardens and rivers, and a row of nameless standing stones.

areas.name: Seven Heavens and Lamp
areas.description: A sun like a lamp and a reflecting moon.

activities.name: Ask forgiveness
activities.description: Carry three rain clouds over three dry fields; they turn green and the river by the gardens fills (an adaptation of the promise in 71:10-12).
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Sun and moon
activities.description: Set the moon on the pedestal for "a [reflected] light" and the sun on the one for "a burning lamp" (71:16).
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: Nuh is not shown or voiced.
learning_objectives: Explain the sun and moon in 71:16

status.playable_environment: first version built: its own scene (fields, gardens and river, sun and moon pedestals, roads) with two hands-on activities in the scene
status.testing: checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL at 960x600; not tested on phones or real GPUs
status.tested_by: automated screenshots of the scene and the in-scene activities

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A walled courtyard in morning sun with a gap in the west wall, mirrors on stands, and a seedling in a dark corner

primary_mechanic.text: Turn four mirrors (slanted either way or tipped flat) until the beam of sunlight from the gap, sent back from mirror to mirror, reaches the seedling in the dark corner (71:16, the moon a light, the sun a lamp; the moon shines with the sun’s light sent back). One mirror must be tipped flat or it throws the light out.

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading by the oaks, the courtyard of light, then a reading on the road out
environment_behaviour: the light beam follows the mirrors as they turn
the seedling grows and glows when the light reaches it
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that Allah made the sun a lamp and the moon a light (71:16)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Patient Messenger
story_library.children_narration: Prophet Nuh encouraged his people to worship Allah and ask for forgiveness. He spoke to them openly and privately, during the day and at night. He reminded them to look at the heavens, the moon, the sun, and the earth. Although many refused to listen, he continued his mission with patience.

world_idea.title: Nuh's Village of Signs
world_idea.description: This world focuses on Nuh's message and long perseverance. Children explore places symbolizing his different appeals, with sky-observation activities. The ark adventure belongs to the wider Nuh story collection, grounded particularly in passages such as Hud 11:37–44, rather than being falsely attributed to Surah Nuh itself.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Agreed with the library: no ark here. The ark story is in Hud (11:37-44).
